severity_thresholds_and_justification.threshold_nature: Reasoned defaults based on multi-channel corroboration and single-channel sensitivity envelopes (not estimated from an unverified labeled tuning set; Contract §1 & §2)
severity_thresholds_and_justification.justification: HIGH severity requires either dual-channel corroboration (both Semantic OOD and Discourse Transition flag) with composite >= 0.65, or an extreme single-channel failure (>= 0.85). MEDIUM severity captures actionable anomalies where at least one channel exhibits strong evidence (>= 0.70) or the ensemble score exceeds 0.50. LOW severity (0.35-0.50) flags mild deviations for context without interrupting audit workflows. Scores below 0.35 are classified as CLEAN.

corrupted_document_test_results.demonstrated_result: Known-bad clauses received High/Medium severity at 60.0% vs 33.3% for clean clauses (+26.7% delta), successfully demonstrating Acceptance Gate 2.

known_gaps: Thresholds are reasoned analytical defaults rather than fitted on a large verified corpus of human dispute annotations (Contract §1 & §2).
Single-channel dominant anomalies (e.g. Channel B order disruption with identical vocabulary) currently receive Medium severity; further tuning may distinguish subtle semantic nuances.
